title: AHB Signoff Evidence Board
description: Select a signoff area to connect the review question to the concrete assertion, coverage, scoreboard, or analysis evidence that should answer it.

signals.name: Reset and first transfer
signals.expansion: Safe reset state and legal restart
signals.description: Confirm address/control return to safe values during reset and that the first valid transfer after release begins legally.
signals.direction: Reset controller, master, and every monitored interface
signals.sampled: Reset assertion, synchronous release edge, and first accepted NONSEQ
signals.typicalUse: Reset assertions plus directed reset-under-traffic tests
signals.verificationNote: Retain a waveform showing reset assertion during an active transfer and the documented recovery behavior.

signals.name: Wait-state behavior
signals.description: Prove that address/control and write-data owners do not advance while their respective phases are stalled.
signals.sampled: Every low-HREADY interval, including long and single-cycle stalls
signals.typicalUse: Stability assertions and constrained wait-state regression
signals.verificationNote: Review assertion exceptions for IDLE, BUSY, and ERROR before accepting a green property report.

signals.name: Burst legality
signals.expansion: Type, size, alignment, count, and boundary
signals.description: Demonstrate legal NONSEQ/SEQ progression for every supported HBURST and HSIZE, including wrap math and the 1 KB boundary.
signals.typicalUse: Burst predictor, assertions, and crossed functional coverage
signals.verificationNote: A coverage hit is insufficient unless the scoreboard/checker also validated every generated address.

signals.name: Response handling
signals.description: Attribute each response to the correct data phase and verify both legal choices after ERROR: cancel the remaining burst or continue it as documented by the master.
signals.verificationNote: Inject ERROR on the first, middle, and final beat and compare actual side effects with the documented recovery policy.

signals.name: End-to-end data
signals.expansion: No loss, duplication, corruption, or misrouting
signals.description: Compare accepted writes and returned reads against an independent reference model across stalls, bursts, errors, and interconnect routes.
signals.verificationNote: Ensure expected and actual streams are not derived from the same monitor logic; correlated bugs can otherwise self-cancel.

signals.name: Version and options
signals.expansion: AHB, AHB-Lite, and declared AHB5 properties
signals.description: Show that the checker, stimulus, and coverage model match the implemented interface revision and optional capabilities.
signals.sampled: Environment build and every option-specific transfer
signals.verificationNote: A checker that assumes absent signals, or ignores declared capabilities, can report misleading signoff.

signals.name: Coverage closure
signals.expansion: Legal holes explained and illegal bins excluded
signals.description: Review every zero-hit legal bin, every exclusion, and every cross that matters to the verification plan.
signals.sampled: After stable regressions with assertion and scoreboard pass rates
signals.verificationNote: Do not use a raw percentage as the decision. Each waiver needs a reason and each critical scenario needs a reproducing test.

signals.name: Progress and performance
signals.expansion: Documented latency, fairness, and deadlock bounds
signals.description: Prove implementation-specific service guarantees under realistic contention and backpressure assumptions.
signals.direction: System contract → liveness properties and stress tests
signals.typicalUse: Formal liveness plus long-running contention tests
signals.verificationNote: Separate a protocol requirement from a product performance promise and record the assumptions used by the proof.
